{{Short description|Statement in elementary geometry}}
{{CS1 config|mode=cs2}}
[[File:Eyeball theorem variation.svg|thumb|upright=1.5|'''Eyeball theorem''': red chords are of equal length.<br/> '''Variant''': blue chords are of equal length.]]
The '''eyeball theorem''' is a statement in elementary geometry about a property of a pair of disjoint [[circle]]s.

More precisely it states the following:<ref>Claudi Alsina, Roger B. Nelsen: ''Icons of Mathematics: An Exploration of Twenty Key Images''. MAA, 2011, ISBN 978-0-88385-352-8, pp.&nbsp;132–133 </ref>
<blockquote>
For two nonintersecting circles <math>c_P</math> and <math>c_Q</math> centered at <math>P</math> and <math>Q</math>, label the points where the [[tangent line]]s from P onto <math>c_Q</math> cross <math>c_P</math> as <math>A</math> and <math>B</math>, and label the points where the tangents from Q onto <math>c_P</math> cross <math>c_Q</math> as <math>C</math> and <math>D</math>. Then <math>|AB| = |CD|</math>.
</blockquote>

The eyeball theorem was discovered in the 1960s by the Peruvian mathematician  Antonio Gutierrez.<ref> David Acheson: ''The Wonder Book of Geometry''. Oxford University Press, 2020, ISBN 9780198846383, pp.&nbsp;141–142</ref> However, without the use of its current name it was already posed and solved as a problem in an article by George W. Evans in 1938.<ref name="Garcia"/> Evans stated that the problem was given in "some examination paper".<ref>{{citation|last=Evans|first=George W.|year=1938|title=Ratio as multiplier|journal=The Mathematics Teacher|volume=31|issue=3|pages=114–116|doi=10.5951/MT.31.3.0114|jstor=27952156}}</ref> 

A related theorem states that if <math>F</math> and <math>J</math> are points of tangency from <math>Q</math> on <math>c_P</math> and from <math>P</math> on <math>c_Q</math> respectively, and one draws line <math>FJ</math> in such a way that it intersects <math>c_P</math> for the second time at <math>F'</math> and <math>c_Q</math> at <math>J'</math>, then <math>|FF'|=|JJ'|</math>.<ref name="Garcia">{{citation
|last=José García |first=Emmanuel Antonio |title=A Variant of the Eyeball Theorem |journal=The College Mathematics Journal |volume=53 |number=2 |year=2022 |pages=147–148|doi=10.1080/07468342.2022.2022905 }}</ref>

Several proofs are known; one derives the theorem from the [[Japanese theorem for cyclic quadrilaterals]].<ref>[https://www.cut-the-knot.org/Curriculum/Geometry/Eyeball.shtml ''The Eyeball Theorem''] at [[Alexander_Bogomolny#Cut-the-Knot|cut-the-knot.org]]</ref>
